name: Padel court
summary: A padel court is a rectangle 20 m long and 10 m wide, measured inside the enclosure, closed in by walls and wire mesh and split in half by a net. The FIP Rules of Padel allow a tolerance of 0.5% on these dimensions.

length.editorNote: Rulebook states 20 m interior length, 0.5% tolerance

width.editorNote: Rulebook states 10 m interior width, 0.5% tolerance

offset.editorNote: Runs along the centre of the court from the net to at least 20 cm beyond the service line

specs.label: Centre service line extends beyond the service line

fact.editorNote: 3 m of wall topped by 1 m of metal mesh

fact.text: Two permitted layouts: stepped walls at each end (3 m high for 2 m, then 2 m high for 2 m), or an unstepped glass wall 3 m high for 4 m; metal mesh completes the sides
fact.editorNote: Corrected from 'Stepped solid walls at each end of the sides, with metal mesh above' on 2026-10-24. Rulebook gives Variant 1 (stepped) and Variant 2 (glass, no step)

name: Padel rules summary
summary: Padel is played in pairs on an enclosed court: the ball must cross the net and bounce once on the opponents' side, after which it may be played off the walls. Scoring follows tennis, with games and sets.

points.text: The server bounces the ball on the ground and strikes it at or below waist height
points.editorNote: Corrected from 'Served underhand, striking the ball at or below waist height after bouncing it on the ground' on 2026-10-24. Rulebook does not use the word underhand

points.text: The server keeps at least one foot on the ground when striking the ball
The serve goes diagonally and must bounce in the receiver's service box
Two attempts are allowed at each serve
Points, games and sets are counted as in tennis: 15, 30, 40, game
At deuce, an event may use advantage, golden point or star point
Golden point: a single deciding point at the first deuce, with the receiving pair choosing which side receives
Star point: up to two advantages are played after deuce, then a single deciding point
After the ball bounces on your side you may play it off your own walls before returning it
A return must bounce in the opponents' court before touching their walls or mesh; it may first come off the hitter's own walls
points.editorNote: Corrected from 'The return must go over the net directly; it may not hit the opponents' walls or mesh before bouncing on their side' on 2026-10-24

points.text: A volley is allowed, except when returning the serve
A point is lost if the ball bounces twice on your side
A point is lost if a player touches the net, or the ball strikes a player, before it is dead
A served ball that bounces in the box and then touches the mesh before the second bounce is a fault
Padel is played as doubles, two against two
Partners alternate serving games in a set order, and each player receives from one side for the whole set

name: Padel
summary: Padel is a racket sport for two pairs, played on a small enclosed court with a net across the middle and walls that keep the ball in play. Players use solid, stringless rackets and a ball similar to a tennis ball, serve underhand, and score as in tennis.

origin.editorNote: Research environment could not open any web page on 2026-10-24 (egress proxy refused every host; only web search was available). The FIP history page (seen only as a search excerpt) credits Enrique Corcuera, who built the first court at his home in Acapulco, Mexico, in 1969. The sport later spread to Spain (Marbella) and Argentina; dates for that differ between sources.

children.text: Padel is played two against two on a small rectangular court that is closed in on all sides. A net divides the court in half, as in tennis, but the ends and parts of the sides are solid walls, with wire mesh making up the rest of the enclosure. Rackets have no strings: they are solid, perforated paddles, and the ball is similar to a tennis ball.

A point starts with an underhand serve, struck after the ball has been bounced, sent diagonally into the opponents' service box. From then on the ball has to cross the net and land on the other side before it touches anything else. Once it has bounced on your side you may let it come off your walls and still play it, which gives rallies their character: much of the game is about reading the rebound rather than hitting winners.

Because the walls return so many shots, padel tends to reward placement, patience and teamwork over raw power. Pairs often build points with lobs and soft balls to the feet, waiting for a chance to finish at the net. Scoring borrows from tennis, with games and sets, although events may choose a deciding point at deuce to keep matches moving.

The game took shape in Mexico and grew first in Spain and Argentina, which remain its heartlands. It has since spread across Europe, the Middle East and the Americas, and an international professional tour now runs under the International Padel Federation.

relatedSports.note: Padel counts points, games and sets as tennis does.
